Rashi on Kiddushin 30b:10:1.hebrew: אלא בתו בידו היא - בתמיה: כלום יכול להרגיל לה אנשים להשיאה, דאמר קרא: "ואת בנותיכם תנו לאנשים":
Rashi on Kiddushin 30b:10:1.english: But [with regard to] his daughter, is it in his power - [This is asked] in astonishment: Is he at all able to attract men to her to marry her, that the verse stated: "And give your daughters to men"?

Rashi on Kiddushin 30b:11:1.hebrew: אמור לחכמה אחותי את - שתהא בקי בה כאחותך שאסורה לך. אי נמי, מסיפא דקרא: ״ומודע לבינה תקרא״ — שתהא ידוע לך:
Rashi on Kiddushin 30b:11:1.english: “Say to wisdom: You are my sister” - That you should be well-versed in it like your sister, who is [clearly] forbidden to you. Alternatively, [it is derived] from the end of the verse: “And call understanding your kinswoman” — that it should be known to you.

Rashi on Kiddushin 30b:11:2.hebrew: ראה חיים - אומנות שתחיה בו. ״עם אשה״ — מקיש אומנות לאשה:
Rashi on Kiddushin 30b:11:2.english: See life - A trade through which you will live. “With a wife” — [the verse] juxtaposes a trade to a wife.

Rashi on Kiddushin 30b:11:3.hebrew: אם אשה - האמור כאן אשה ממש היא: כשם שמצינו שחייב אדם להשיאו אשה, כך חייב כו':
Rashi on Kiddushin 30b:11:3.english: If [the] woman - mentioned here is an actual woman: Just as we find that a person is obligated to marry him to a woman, so too is he obligated, etc.

Rashi on Kiddushin 30b:14:1.hebrew: מאי בינייהו - מאי קא מוסיף ר' יהודה:
Rashi on Kiddushin 30b:14:1.english: What is [the difference] between them - What is Rabbi Yehuda adding?

Rashi on Kiddushin 30b:14:2.hebrew: עיסקא - אם למדו סחורה: לת"ק — הרי למדו חיים; לרבי יהודה, דאתי לטעמא — אומנות דוקא, דכמה פעמים שאין לו במה לעשות סחורה, ועומד ומלסטם:
Rashi on Kiddushin 30b:14:2.english: Business - If he taught him commerce: According to the first tanna, behold, he has taught him “life”; [but] according to Rabbi Yehuda, who comes to [provide] the rationale, [he must teach him] specifically a trade, for there are many times when he has nothing with which to conduct business, and he will resort to banditry.

Rashi on Kiddushin 30b:15:1.hebrew: דמיחייב אבא למיעבד לברא - כגון למולו ולפדותו. והכי משמע מתני': כל מצות שהאב מצווה על מעשה הבן:
Rashi on Kiddushin 30b:15:1.english: That a father is obligated to perform for his son - Such as to circumcise him and to redeem him. And this is what the Mishnah means: All mitzvot that the father is commanded regarding actions concerning the son.

Rashi on Kiddushin 30b:16:1.english: That is incumbent upon the son - Such as honoring and revering [one's parents].

Rashi on Kiddushin 30b:17:1.english: [It is in his] power - Ability, for there is no one who protests against him:

Rashi on Kiddushin 30b:17:2.english: The authority of another - Her husband.

Rashi on Kiddushin 30b:17:3.hebrew: נתגרשה - מבעלה, הרי היא כאחיה במצות כיבוד:
Rashi on Kiddushin 30b:17:3.english: [If] she is divorced - From her husband, she is like her brother regarding the mitzvah of honoring [parents].

Rashi on Kiddushin 30b:1:1.hebrew: אמור לחכמה אחותי את - שתהא בקי בה כאחותך שאסורה לך. אי נמי, מסיפא דקרא: "ומודע לבינה תקרא" — שתהא ידוע לך:
Rashi on Kiddushin 30b:1:1.english: “Say to wisdom: You are my sister” - That you should be [as] well-versed in it as [you are certain that] your sister is forbidden to you. Alternatively, [the derivation is] from the end of the verse: “And call understanding your kinswoman” — that it should be known to you.

Rashi on Kiddushin 30b:1:2.english: As arrows in the hand of a mighty man - Who fights with them against his enemies.

Rashi on Kiddushin 30b:1:3.hebrew: כן בני הנעורים - תלמידיו של אדם, הקרויין בניו, כמו שאמר יחזקיהו (ד"ה ב כט): ״בני עתה אל תשלו״; ואומר: ״הנה אנכי והילדים אשר נתן לי וגו'״ (ישעיהו ח׳:י״ח):
Rashi on Kiddushin 30b:1:3.english: So are the children of one’s youth - A person’s disciples, who are called his children, just as Hezekiah said (II Chronicles 29:11): “My sons, do not now be negligent”; and it states: “Behold, I and the children whom [the Lord] has given me...” (Isaiah 8:18).

Rashi on Kiddushin 30b:1:4.hebrew: אשר מלא את אשפתו מהם - משום דדמינהו לחצים, נקט לשון מילוי אשפה:
Rashi on Kiddushin 30b:1:4.english: Who has filled his quiver with them - Because he compared them to arrows, he used the expression of filling a quiver.

Rashi on Kiddushin 30b:1:5.english: With enemies in the gate - This is the end of [the verse,] “Happy is the man.”

Rashi on Kiddushin 30b:20:1.hebrew: ודאי בהכאה אי אפשר - להקישה, שאין הכאה כלפי מעלה:
Rashi on Kiddushin 30b:20:1.english: It is certainly impossible with regard to striking - To compare it, for there is no striking toward [God on] High.

Rashi on Kiddushin 30b:21:1.hebrew: וכן בדין - שיוקשו לכיבוד ומורא על הבן, שהרי אף הן שותפין למקום בו:
Rashi on Kiddushin 30b:21:1.english: And so [it is] logical - That they should be equated with regard to honor and reverence [incumbent] upon the son, for they too are partners with the Omnipresent in him:

Rashi on Kiddushin 30b:21:2.hebrew: שלשה שותפין הן - מפרש בברייתא במסכת נדה: איש מזריע לובן שבו, אשה מזרעת אודם שבו, והקדוש ברוך הוא נופח בו נשמה, מראה עין, ושמיעת אוזן, ודיבור:
Rashi on Kiddushin 30b:21:2.english: There are three partners - It is explained in a baraita in Tractate Niddah: The man emits the white [substance] in him, the woman emits the red [substance] in him, and the Holy One, Blessed be He, breathes into him a soul, sight of the eye, hearing of the ear, and speech.

Rashi on Kiddushin 30b:2:1.hebrew: נעשו אויבים - מתוך שמקשים זה לזה, ואין זה מקבל דברי זה:
Rashi on Kiddushin 30b:2:1.english: They become enemies - Because they raise difficulties against one another, and this one does not accept the words of that one.

Rashi on Kiddushin 30b:2:2.hebrew: את והב בסופה - הכי דריש לה: ספר מלחמות — מלחמה שעל ידי ספר, אהבה יש בסופה:
Rashi on Kiddushin 30b:2:2.english: Vahev in Suphah - This is how he expounds it: “The book of the wars” — [regarding] a war that is [waged] by means of a book, there is love at its end.

Rashi on Kiddushin 30b:3:1.hebrew: ושמתם את דברי אלה סם תם - שלם, שאינו חסר שום הצלה:
Rashi on Kiddushin 30b:3:1.english: “And you shall place these words of Mine” — a perfect elixir - Complete, which does not lack any [measure of] deliverance:

Rashi on Kiddushin 30b:3:2.hebrew: מה שהנאתך - כל מה שדעתך נוחה הימנו, ואפי' דבש וכל מיני מתיקה שקשים למכה:
Rashi on Kiddushin 30b:3:2.english: Whatever you enjoy - Anything that you find pleasing, and even honey and all kinds of sweets, which are harmful to a wound.

Rashi on Kiddushin 30b:3:3.hebrew: נומי - צמחים, בורפיליו"ש (בורבולי"ש: אבעבועות, כיבים) בלע"ז:
Rashi on Kiddushin 30b:3:3.english: Ulcers [nomi] - Sores; borfilios (borboles: blisters, boils) in Old French.

Rashi on Kiddushin 30b:4:1.english: If you do well - [Through the] “good teaching” [i.e., the Torah, as it is stated: “For I have given you good teaching; do not forsake My Torah” (Proverbs 4:2)].

Rashi on Kiddushin 30b:4:2.english: Lifted up - You will elevate yourself above your [evil] inclination.

Rashi on Kiddushin 30b:5:1.english: Its dealings - [The dealings] of the evil inclination are with man, to cause him to sin.

Rashi on Kiddushin 30b:5:2.hebrew: ואם אתה רוצה - עסוק בתורה, ואתה מושל בו:
Rashi on Kiddushin 30b:5:2.english: And if you wish - Engage in Torah [study], and you will rule over it.

Rashi on Kiddushin 30b:6:1.hebrew: כל היום - קרא יתירא הוא, ללמדנו שכל שעות היום רעתו מתחדשת:
Rashi on Kiddushin 30b:6:1.english: All day - It is a superfluous verse, to teach us that throughout all hours of the day its evil is renewed.

Rashi on Kiddushin 30b:8:1.english: This wretched one - The evil inclination provokes you.

Rashi on Kiddushin 30b:8:2.hebrew: מתפוצץ - שהתורה כאש נמשלה, המפעפע את הברזל:
Rashi on Kiddushin 30b:8:2.english: It will shatter - For the Torah is compared to fire, which penetrates the iron.

Tosafot on Kiddushin 30b:17:1.hebrew: שיש רשות אחרים עליה - ואע"ג דמעשה ידיה לבעלה מדרבנן בעלמא, מ"מ אינה מצויה אצל אביה, אלא אצל בעלה:
Tosafot on Kiddushin 30b:17:1.english: "Because she is under the authority of another" - And even though [the rule that] her earnings belong to her husband is merely Rabbinic, nevertheless she is not found with her father, but rather with her husband.

Tosafot on Kiddushin 30b:8:1.hebrew: אם ברזל הוא מתפוצץ - תימה, דהא קרא משמע שהפטיש מפוצץ סלע ומשברו! וכן קשה בפרק דיני ממונות (סנהדרין דף לד.), דקאמר: "מה פטיש מתחלק לכמה ניצוצות, אף דברי תורה מתחלק לכמה טעמים", ושם גריס רשב"ם "מחלק", ול"ג "מתחלק". ויש שגורס כאן: "אם ברזל הוא מפעפע, ואם סלע הוא מתפוצץ, שנאמר: 'הלא כה דברי כאש וכפטיש יפוצץ סלע' — שהאש מפעפע הברזל, והפטיש מפוצץ את הסלע". ור"ת מפרש שהסלע משבר את הברזל, וה"ק: "וכפטיש יפוצץ" — מכח סלע, כדאמר במדרש: מעשה באחד שלקח סנפירינון לבודקו, נתנו על הסדן והכה בקורנס; נשבר הקורנס ונחלק הסדן, והסנפירינון לא זז ממקומו:
Tosafot on Kiddushin 30b:8:1.english: "If it is iron, it shatters" - [This is] astonishing, for the verse implies that the hammer shatters a rock and breaks it! And similarly, it is difficult in the chapter [entitled] Dinei Mamonot (Sanhedrin 34a), where [the Gemara] says: "Just as a hammer divides into several sparks, so too the words of Torah divide into several meanings." And there, Rashbam reads "divides" [meḥallek], and does not read "is divided" [mitḥallek]. And some read here: "If it is iron, it dissolves, and if it is rock, it shatters, as it is stated: 'Is not My word like fire, and like a hammer that shatters rock?' — for fire dissolves iron, and the hammer shatters the rock." And Rabbeinu Tam explains that the rock breaks the iron, and this is what it means: "And like a hammer [that] shatters" — by the force of the rock. As [the Sages] said in the Midrash: An incident occurred with someone who took a sapphire [stone] to test it; he placed it on the anvil and struck it with a hammer — the hammer broke and the anvil split, but the sapphire did not budge from its place.
